newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's human rights chief calls for gay rights.
newsitem.headline: Australia's human rights chief calls for gay rights.

text.p: Australia's human rights commissioner on Tuesday called for national laws to ensure equality for homosexuals, claiming gay men and women were denied their full civil rights and faced an alarming level of violence.

"Australia's international human rights commitments require Australia to take all necessary measures to eliminate discrimination, including discrimination on the grounds of sexual orientation and transgender identity," Chris Sidoti said.
He said some Australians laws continued to deny homosexuals their "full civil rights" because of their sexual orientation.
"This situation is not acceptable," said Sidoti. "These rights are not granted or created. They are entitlements arising from our common humanity and inherent dignity."
"By failing to properly address on-going discrimination we not only contradict Australia's national ethos of a 'fair go', but also fail to meet our international human rights obligations," he said.
Sidoti said two of Australia's six states, Tasmania and Western Australia, had failed to introduce laws prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual preference or lawful sexual activity.
Tasmania's anti-homosexual laws carry jail terms of up to 21 years. The laws describe the act of homosexuality as "unnatural sexual intercourse" and makes it illegal in public or private.
In 1994 a U.N. human rights committee ruled the Tasmanian laws breach privacy provisions under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.
In Western Australia the age of consent for a male homosexual is 21, compared with 16-18 in the rest of Australia.

Sidoti said same sex couples were also denied the legal entitlements available to heterosexual couples such as bearevement leave, careers leave, superannuation payments, compensation rights, tax concessions and property rights.
Sidoti also said, "Violence against lesbians, gay men and transgenders is occuring with alarming regularity and public harassment and verbal abuse are not uncommon experiences."
Stevie Clayton, from the Gay and Lesbian Rights Lobby, said 25 gay men had been murdered in Australia because of their sexual orientation in the past five years.
On Saturday, hundreds of thousands of people packed central Sydney for the city's annual Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras parade, the end of a month of events celebrating homosexuality.
